correctness.rationale: The interval-propagation lemma proves first-move forcing on every path power for all n≥2 and 1≤k<n, treating truncated neighborhoods. Proper forcing sets without first moves cannot advance; every forcing set contains an oriented-edge trigger. For squares, a complete boundary/interior trigger census and antichain deletion yields exactly four size-two patterns, one/two size-three patterns, and three n−7 size-four families for n≥8. Embedded verifier independently tests 163716 initial masks for general powers and 524280 square masks; finite tests corroborate the rigorous proof, not replace it.

The 2022 minimal-set primary paper addresses general structural and extremal properties, and the 2018 polynomial paper addresses ordinary paths and other families. The 2025 skew forcing study has a different forcing rule. No exact covering statement was found in actual scholarly literature and semantic records; priority remains provisional because unindexed equivalents and other general forcing theorems are possible.

value.rationale: For all powers of paths, a dynamical reachability property is reduced to a single local initial-move predicate, giving a compact trigger hypergraph and a direct characterization of all starting configurations. The exact P_n^2 antichain polynomial enumerates all labelled inclusion-minimal forcing sets, separating the pre-known size-two optimum from size-three and size-four irredundant configurations and identifying the first parameter thresholds. This structural classification and count do not follow from the known extremal zero forcing number.
